Accepts.description:
How a pack takes the images a call references: by path on the shared filesystem or as
base64 PNG bytes inside `_harness`.

dir.description: The directory, created when first used.

CheckerConfig.description:
`[checker]`: a table-manners tool action that answers with a verdict (table-manners 2.4),
called as `<command> --arguments <file> --allow-dir <dir>` with `arguments` rendered:
every string value's `{source}`, `{candidate}` and `{prompt}` replaced by the input image's
staged path, the result's staged path and the call's prompt. The arguments are the checker's
own, so rascal holds no checker-specific code. `key_env` names the checker's key: declared so
readiness lists it (optional, for checking the result) and a host passes it; never read,
stored or logged, and kept from every pack.

arguments.description: The checker's call arguments, with the placeholders in its string values.

command.description:
The command and its arguments, by absolute path (a host runs tools with a fixed `PATH`);
rascal adds `--arguments <file>` and `--allow-dir <dir>`.

key_env.description: The environment variable holding the checker's key.

revision.description: Free text naming what the checker is (its version, its model), recorded with each check.

spend_usd_per_call.description:
The most one check may cost, in US dollars: reserved per try and passed as the call's
`max_spend_usd`.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before a check is abandoned (the check could not run).

manifest.description: The corpus manifest; relative to the configuration file.

FillerConfig.description:
One filler entry under `[fillers.<name>]`: a command with placeholders or an HTTP endpoint,
the rendering profile it takes, the paste mode its result is composited with, a timeout,
and for the lab a revision string. `key_env` names the environment variable holding the
filler's key, which is read at call time and never stored, logged or journaled.

command.description:
The command and its arguments; `{image}`, `{mask}`, `{out}` and `{prompt}` are
substituted. Exactly one of `command` and `url`.

fill_max_side.description:
The longest side of the request this filler is sent: a larger support goes downscaled
to fit and the fill comes back scaled to the support (a scaled window, for a model
trained small, such as LaMa). Unset: the request is the support's size.

key_env.description:
The environment variable holding the filler's key: sent as the bearer for `url`; for a
`command`, declared so readiness lists it and a host passes it (the command inherits
rascal's environment). Kept from every pack either way.

max_side.description: The filler's largest side; the heal graph windows to it. Unset: no window.

overrides.description:
Recipe overrides `heal` applies when this filler paints, `"<step>.<param>" = value` or
`"<step>.constants" = "<set>"` (the matrix's form): the band a filler can carry is a
property of the filler (`docs/results/seam-02.md`). `rascal run` and the lab ignore
them: a run without a filler has none, and a lab arm says everything it runs.

paste.description: The paste mode for its result: `feather`, `hard` or `poisson`.

profile.description:
The rendering profile the filler takes: `grey` or `binary` (mask input), `alpha` or
`tinted` (image input).

revision.description: Free text the lab hashes into a cell's identity; required for lab use.

send_mask.description: For an image-input profile: also send the `grey` rendering as `mask`.

spend_usd_per_call.description:
What one call to this filler costs, in US dollars: the run's estimated spend
(table-manners 2.3). Unset: free.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before the call is abandoned as an operational error.

url.description:
The endpoint of a multipart POST (`image`, `mask` when the profile has one, `prompt`
when given) that answers with a PNG.

LimitsConfig.description:
`[limits]`: what a call and a server session may spend, in US dollars, by the fillers'
configured prices. Unset: no limit.

call_cap_usd.description: The most one call may spend; a call may lower it, never raise it.

session_budget_usd.description: The most a `serve` process may spend across its calls.

Override.description: An override's value: what a step parameter takes.

PackConfig.description:
One tool pack under `[packs.<name>]`: the command that serves MCP over stdio, the
environment it may see beyond the baseline, how it takes images, whether it may run calls at
once, a revision string for the lab, and two timeouts.

call_timeout_s.description: Seconds before a call is abandoned as an operational error and the pack shut down.

command.description: The command and its arguments; no placeholders.

concurrent.description: Whether calls may run at once; effective only when the tool's manifest agrees.

env.description:
Environment variable names passed through in addition to the baseline (`PATH`, `HOME`,
`LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TMPDIR`). A name any filler uses as `key_env`, or one ending in
`_KEY`, `_TOKEN` or `_SECRET`, is removed even when declared.

revision.description: Free text the lab hashes into a cell's identity; required for lab use.

startup_timeout_s.description: Seconds for the process to answer `initialize` and list its tools.

ServeConfig.description:
`[serve]`: `allow_dirs` narrows the directories `rascal serve --allow-dir` allows, never
widens them (PLAN.md 10.1): where a listed directory and a flag directory overlap the deeper
one is allowed, a listed directory under no flag allows nothing, and `[]` allows nothing.

allow_dirs.description: Absolute directories; unset, the flags stand as given.

runs.description:
Where the contract's action runs go when `--runs` is not given, relative to this file;
unset, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/rascal/runs`. With `[workspace] dir`, a host can start
`rascal serve --config <file>` alone, and `rascal call --config <file>` from a terminal
then uses the same workspace and runs.

WorkspaceConfig.description: Where runs keep their workspace when `--workspace` is not given.

dir.description: A directory; relative to the configuration file.

cache.description:
The fill cache (table-manners 4.4, ADR 0020): a fill is kept by its request, so an
identical request is answered without calling the filler again.

checker.description: The tool `heal remove-prompt` asks whether the object is gone (ADR 0023); at most one.
